components.gap: Not reconstructed: (a) section 4.3's claim that the maxmin rule LP(f)>=LP(g) resolves the Ellsberg paradox while the dominance rule on LP(f-g) satisfies Savage's sure-thing principle (handbook 467-475 and annex 170-182 only show the two rules differ); (b) the Cox critique that postulate (i) is natural only if Bayes conditioning is presupposed, and Paris's replacement of condition (iii) by strict monotonicity of F (handbook 327-329 says only 'additional infinite/density assumptions'); the use of Cox in the AI literature (Horvitz-Heckerman-Langlotz, Cheeseman, Jaynes) and Lindley's uniqueness principle are not presented; (c) section 2.1's argument that additivity is natural for frequencies of repeatable events but not for degrees of belief attached to unique events; (d) the source's claim that any convex set of probabilities is representable by lower previsions on some gamble family is not stated as such.
